summary: Case B: the complete frozen H1 remains inconclusive in the common and longest main-view arms without forced conditions. Its unchanged requirement is a ratio CI strictly above one at every evaluable input, no supported reversal, and non-overlapping size noise-tolerance CIs; weak-to-intermediate gains alone do not satisfy it. At input 0.003, the rate ratios are 19.12, 11.00, 7.55 for Wave-pinning, Holmes and Spring; at 0.05 they are 4.63, 2.53, 1.18, with geometric-normalized ratios 0.51, 0.28, 0.14 and multiple-front majorities. Thus resolved size gains can coexist with erosion below the single-front geometric expectation, while Spring's 0.05 ratio CI includes one. Main-view size noise-tolerance CIs separate in these three models. Goryachev remains coverage/lag/forcing qualified. Updated H2 model calls are reported, but H2 overall retains its legacy direct-time A6 predictor gate, and H3 retains its legacy time-bound definition; neither is a fully revalidated rate-based hypothesis. Stop for review before rebuilding the Figure 4 main.
qualifications: All 308 S0 rows cover both arms, all seven views, and both forcing choices; old calls appear alongside updated calls.
Frozen H1 applies to every evaluable input, with at least three of four models required overall; no weak-input-only gate was introduced.

The authorized fhalf substitution uses absolute heading autocorrelation 0.5 at the fixed reference lag, replacing the historical weakest-input-relative tolerance; the original authority text is retained verbatim as provenance.
H2 overall is a mixed-estimand replay with the frozen legacy direct-tau A6 predictor gate, not a new-rate predictor validation.
H3 is retained as its legacy tauStrong/tauWeak empirical-bound result; a new-rate H3 was not defined or validated.
Geometric normalization is relative to the single-front expectation, is not site diffusivity, and is not a decision gate.
Non-exponential lag dependence, unavailable exact saved-time lags, forced states, and one-sided bounds remain explicit in the metric tables.
The association between multiple fronts and diminished geometric advantage is descriptive, not an independently validated causal or predictive claim.
The modeled activity heading is distinct from observed migration summaries and conditional OU persistence estimates.
